chapter: Parker, Buster Smith and the Kansas City style
title: Blues hits and Kansas City jazz as revival meeting
summary: Dance cites hit blues by Ellington; Ramey says Kansas City jazz imitates camp meeting revivals.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: That simple blues is it. But, what I wanted to say, when we were describing the jazz and different phases of jazz, like the New Orleans jazz, Chicago jazz, now, a camp meeting - we all look upon Kansas City jazz as like completely imitated from one of those revival meetings, where the preacher and the people are singing, all that living, and there's happenings all around, (unintelligible) and everything. So we always think of Kansas City jazz as something like that, it's something you're bound to feel.
